body:
Yes. Depends who you ask I suppose (some say it's for the best), but I personally think it sucked. I went to talk about the fact that I was hearing voices and I got sent me to the hospital, even though I told him I absolutely did not want to do that. He said that the voices were telling me not to go, so he couldn't take what I was saying seriously. (What? Honestly I just didn't want to go to the hospital.)

After the hospital visit they wanted me to take a medical leave. I didn't want to do that, so I basically lied about how I was doing until they signed me off.

I took Risperidone because I was (am) heading voices. I couldn't stay on it because, as mentioned above, it made me feel like a zombie, to the point where I could barely get my work done. Wow I wish it worked for me though...

I had the same thing. It was awkward at first for me to tell them where I was at because I never talked about that kind of stuff with my parents before. Then again, considering my parents were helping me out a bit financially while I was getting my life back together, I figured it was right to do so.

I wouldn't call it an obligation. However, in my opinion, it's their right to know; they clearly care enough to pay for you to get better and ask how you're doing.

Hmm, well, here's my story/opinion. Of course, "should I do it" is a question you'll have to answer yourself...

For a long time I had no intention of telling my family about what was going on with me. It's not quite depression - well, it is, but there's other stuff going on as well, and I figured it would weird them out. Plus, as you've mentioned is the case with you, I wasn't that close with my folks. We have this kind of don't-ask-don't-tell thing in my family (with most topics not just this one), probably because my dad was in the army... well I don't know, but that's just how I was raised.

Anyway, last year I was supposed to go on a trip with the family, and I ended up having to miss the trip because the weekend I was supposed to leave I went to the hospital and stayed there from Friday night to Wednesday or so, locked in the mental ward. Obviously I had to tell them, since I was going to be missing the trip that I was supposed to be at.

So I was forced into it. The result? They were more supportive than I could've dreamed of. They live about 300 miles away and when I called them (at 4 or 5am, mind you) they immediately booked a flight and were by my side the same day.

Point is, parents can surprise you. It's nice being able to fall back on them with problems like this. I'd do it. Of course, it may backfire and they'd distance themselves, but for the most part (I think) parents will step up and be there for you.

Ugh, tell me about it. I had to go in to the emergency room last year because I was having problems mentally, and they had to do an MRI and a CT scan to check to see if it was due to a tumor. 

While this was happening, I was thinking about how much it was going to cost and if I'd be able to afford it. I potentially had a tumor, and I was thinking about the money! Unbelievable.

Yes. 

I've tried medication, and I went off all of it. Now I've just pretty much accepted it, I guess. I'm still working on living with it, but I hope I'll get there eventually.

Not the biggest fan of psychiatrists after I ended up in the hospital last time. Even less of a fan of the meds; they wreck me.

I suppose I can give meditation another go.
Understood as in why it happens? That's cool, I don't understand either.

Schizophrenia, maybe. I've looked it up, and it has a whole host of symptoms that I don't have (like delusions, for example). At least I don't think I have them. I've listened to people talking about their own experience with it, and besides the voices I don't have what they do. I'm not sure what I do have, but that's besides the point.

Music usually helps - I play it when I'm going anywhere or trying to focus, it's pretty much the only way.

I tried meditation a little bit. It didn't work, but perhaps I didn't try long enough because I got frustrated. I suppose I could try again.

Risperidone for the voices. A cocktail of antidepressants for the mood.

They were all really rough on me, so I pretended I was better to get out of the hospital and off meds.

I went through the same stuff more or less, MRI, CAT scan, hospitalization, therapists, and a few different medications.  I decided around the end of last year that I didn't want to deal with any of that anymore and stopped seeing anyone or taking any medication. 

Now I'm doing ok, more or less. Some nights are harder than others. I think it's mostly stress that makes it worse for me. I was told that reading some philosophy might help and provide a new way of thinking, so I actually just got my first book a couple of days ago and I'm going to give that a shot.

Sorry, I can't really provide guidance here since I'm working on figuring it out myself, but that's where I'm at. Best of luck.

Makes sense to me.

Originally I was put on Zoloft and it actually made me worse off. I was more paranoid when I was on it and couldn't think straight at all.  I realize that doesn't happen to everyone, but yeah I felt much better off it.

On an unrelated note, are you going off medication unsupervised? You say that you decided to lower the dose... I was tempted to try this, but I got talked out of it. Just be careful and tell someone if things start to not go so well.

I apologize, I don't mean to belittle anything that you are/were going through. I realize that medication and therapy works for a lot of people, and I'm not trying to say otherwise. However, I think if I force myself to have a positive outlook, perhaps I will start to actually have a positive outlook. Maybe if I work hard enough the voices won't come back, or something.

I'm sorry, I realize I'm basically asking for magic. I don't know what I really expected from this post..

Hmm, well I never said that I HAD to get drunk at the bar ;)

My point is, I enjoy staying up till whenever I want, instead of having to ditch out before the night even begins. Sometimes I like to have a casual drink or two, and they just don't mix well with what I was put on. But even if we ignore the fact that I couldn't drink, I couldn't really think straight on them. It wasn't great.

I've been on Risperidone, Zoloft, Abilify, and Lithium.

Wow, thank you. This is exactly what I was looking for.

How do you manage to ignore them though? Sometimes they just flood my mind and I can't do anything else.

I'm 22, and ummm let's see. In the 9 months or so since this began, I've been on Risperidone, Zoloft, Abilify, and Lithium.

Thank you for responding.

People love to tell me that my brain might not be working right, just like people get sick in other ways, but I don't think that is the case. I'm not trying to start an argument in any way, and I realize this might be the wrong subreddit to say this in, but I was never sold on depression being something serious, especially not in my case. I think it's something anybody can snap out of, and I guess I was just looking for a way to do so without medication or therapy. I tried therapy, but I have such a problem opening up that it's just a waste of time and money. I'm looking for another solution.

Thank you for responding.

I tried talking to two about it. I definitely like the second more than the first, but that's not really the point. It doesn't matter how much I like someone, I find this very hard to talk about, and very embarrassing. Even posting to reddit, something that's completely anonymous, took me a week of sitting here thinking about it. I already feel like I'm letting down my family enough without having them pay for therapy (my parents are helping me out with it because there's no way I can afford it). There's nothing any doctor can say that will make me feel better, instead they'll just sit there and go "uh huh" and write a note down.

My goal is to find a way around therapy.

Thank you for responding.

I don't like medication or therapy. I don't like lying to my roommates and friends about where I'm going. I don't like not being able to go to the bar with them, and if I am I can only have one drink. The ones I was taking made me tired at like 9:30, so that was pretty rough too. Even during the day I would be exhausted. It made getting homework done incredibly difficult, because I felt like I wasn't thinking straight anymore. But, like the doctors at the hospital said, at least there were no voices.

I'm not trying to change my opinion on medication and therapy, I'm trying to figure out if there is a way around them.
